rows: Filial piety (xiao), care in old age
The ineffable ground and process of all reality. Not a god, not a person. The way things naturally flow.
Non-forcing action — acting in accord with the natural grain of things. Effortless effectiveness. Not passivity.
Virtue through proper relationships and ritual. Government by moral example. Self-cultivation of ren through li.
Benevolence/humaneness — the supreme Confucian virtue. Realized through proper relations and ritual. The fullest expression of what it means to be human.
An awe-inspiring spirit/force. Can be in natural phenomena, places, or persons. Not "gods" in the Western sense — more like sacred presences.
State Shinto (1868-1945) used kami veneration and emperor worship as nationalist ideology. Yasukuni Shrine remains a live diplomatic issue.
Confucianism, Daoism, Buddhism as complementary rather than competing. Each addresses different aspects of life. The same person can practice all three.
